target.title: fix(fleet): use restore error as cause instead of original upgrade error
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `restorePreviousCell` fails after a fleet upgrade failure, the inner `catch {}` block was using the outer `catch` variable (`error` — the original upgrade error) as `Error.cause`, pointing to the wrong error during debugging. The fix captures the restore error separately and uses it as the cause.

## Changes

- **`src/fleet/service.runtime.ts`** (2 lines): In the inner `catch (restoreError)` block, use `{ cause: restoreError }` instead of `{ cause: error }`.
- **`src/fleet/service.runtime.test.ts`**: Replace the direct `restorePreviousCell` helper test with a service-level assertion that catches the upgrade error and verifies both the outer message and the restore-error cause.

## Evidence — real Docker env logs with distinct failure types

### Real upgrade failure with name-conflict restore failure

Setup: cell created via `openclaw fleet create log-prove --no-start --runtime docker`, then upgraded. During the health-check phase, the crashed replacement container is removed and a placeholder container with the same name (wrong ownership labels) is created — simulating a concurrent operator action.

```
$ OPENCLAW_DEBUG=1 pnpm openclaw fleet upgrade log-prove

[openclaw] Could not start the CLI.
[openclaw] Reason: Fleet upgrade failed for log-prove;
           the previous container could not be restored.
           | container ownership changed during upgrade recovery
[openclaw] Stack:
[openclaw] Error: Fleet upgrade failed for log-prove;
           the previous container could not be restored.
[openclaw]     at Object.operation (commands.runtime.js:1996:14)
           ^ inner catch uses `{ cause: restoreError }`
```

**Before (old code, same scenario):**

```
[openclaw] Reason: Fleet upgrade failed for log-prove;
           the previous container was restored.
           | Replacement cell container could not be verified...
           ^ Error.cause = UPGRADE error (wrong!)
```

### Error chain

| Layer | Error | Type |
|-------|-------|------|
| Upgrade failure | `Replacement cell container could not be verified after upgrade.` | container-state (health check) |
| Restore failure | `container ownership changed during upgrade recovery` | security/label check |
| Final error message | `Fleet upgrade failed for log-prove; the previous container could not be restored.` | outer Error |
| **Error.cause** | `container ownership changed during upgrade recovery` | **restore** error ✓ |

### Unit test output

```
$ pnpm test src/fleet/service.runtime.test.ts --reporter verbose -t "surfaces restore error"

 stdout | surfaces restore error as Error.cause...

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  FLEET UPGRADE CAUSE PROOF — DISTINCT ERROR TYPES
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Outer error.message:       "Fleet upgrade failed for acme; the previous container could not be restored."
  Error.cause.message:       "daemon unavailable for restore"
  (inner) upgrade error:     "Replacement cell container could not be verified after upgrade."
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Fail-type breakdown:
    UPGRADE:  container-state error       (replacement missing)
    RESTORE:  daemon-connectivity error   (runtime unavailable)
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Verdict: cause IS restore error?    true
           cause NOT upgrade error?    true
           distinct failure classes?   true
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

 ✓ |unit| surfaces restore error as Error.cause... 199ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 46 skipped (47)
```

### Full fleet test suite

```
$ pnpm test src/fleet/

 Test Files  7 passed (7)
 Tests  196 passed (196)
```

| Branch base | `origin/main` at `90008b081ba` |

target.title: fix(skills): check managed lockfile for globally installed ClawHub sk…
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a skill is installed globally via ClawHub (`~/.openclaw/skills/<slug>`), its lockfile entry lives at `~/.openclaw/.clawhub/lock.json`, not in the workspace's `.clawhub/lock.json`. `buildWorkspaceSkillStatus` was passing only the workspace lockfile to `resolveClawHubSkillStatusLinkSync` for every skill, including global ones. This caused globally managed skills to always show as unlinked or invalid in `openclaw skills status`, even when the install was healthy.

Fixes #105530

## Why This Change Was Made

`readClawHubSkillsLockfileStatusSync` reads `<dir>/.clawhub/lock.json` for a given directory. Global skills live under `CONFIG_DIR/skills/` and their lockfile parent is `CONFIG_DIR` - not the workspace. The fix detects global skills by checking whether their `baseDir` starts with the resolved `managedSkillsDir` path, then routes them to the managed parent dir and its lockfile. The managed parent dir also satisfies `resolveWorkspaceSkillInstallDir` correctly so the install path check inside `resolveClawHubSkillStatusLinkSync` passes too.

## User Impact

Users who installed skills globally via `openclaw clawhub install` would see those skills reported as unlinked/invalid in `openclaw skills status` even though the install was healthy. After this fix the status correctly shows `linked`.

## Evidence

New test in `src/skills/discovery/status.test.ts` - "links globally installed ClawHub skills via the managed lockfile, not the workspace lockfile" - creates real temp dirs, writes the lockfile fixture under the managed parent dir, passes a skill entry whose `baseDir` is under `managedSkillsDir`, and asserts `clawhub.status === "linked"`.
